remainingFollowUps.title: Evaluate a verified wallet-history checkpoint to reduce repeated lifetime reads
remainingFollowUps.acceptance: Measure long-history lookup and purchase costs before changing the accounting path. Any checkpoint must remain branch/student scoped, reconcile with immutable transactions, account for late imports/corrections/refunds, and share the same concurrency guard as purchases. Retain a bounded reconciliation path and all history; do not replace real receipt evidence with a cached balance.
remainingFollowUps.completionEvidence: 10 November evaluation: one live ledger query returns 2 versus 2,000 history entries in synthetic lookup, with zero writes and older refunds included. Existing purchase tests prove one authoritative scan, atomic guards and no duplicate sale on retry. A checkpoint is deliberately not implemented until every wallet writer participates in its shared revision/cursor and late-correction reconciliation; current account query can also read same-account non-wallet rows before filtering. See docs/advance-credit-navigation-vendor-pass-2026-11-10.md and tests/vendor-remaining-read-cost.test.mjs.

remainingFollowUps.title: Evaluate safe local-network/offline purchases before enabling them
remainingFollowUps.acceptance: Compare measured online costs with a coordinated local-server or explicitly bounded offline allowance design. Define authority, device limits, conflict handling and replay-safe synchronization so two disconnected tills cannot spend the same wallet funds or stock. Keep offline financial posting disabled until the design and failure tests justify it.
remainingFollowUps.completionEvidence: 10 November decision documented in docs/advance-credit-navigation-vendor-pass-2026-11-10.md: retain online authority. Independent disconnected tills cannot validate shared balance/stock; any future offline design needs centrally reserved device allowances and stock, signed journals, deterministic replay and reconciliation. No offline financial posting was enabled.
